bull.b: High gross, operating, and net margins indicate a resilient aftermarket model with pricing power and operating discipline. Management is also guiding to 51.5%–52% gross margin and 19.3%–19.8% operating profit, supporting medium-term margin durability.

Strong professional demand and continued store expansion broaden O’Reilly’s market reach and improve parts availability. The distribution network and commercial delivery model can deepen relationships with repair shops, supporting recurring demand and share gains.

Strong free cash flow provides internal funding for stores, distribution capacity, inventory, and shareholder returns. The year-over-year improvement also gives management flexibility to invest through the cycle, although cash conversion remains below earlier levels.

bear.b: Persistent negative equity and increasing debt create a structurally weaker financial position and reduce flexibility during demand or margin pressure. The capital structure also makes leverage metrics less informative and heightens refinancing and interest-burden risk.

Revenue growth has decelerated materially from prior years, while weaker DIY transaction counts indicate pressure on a major customer channel. Sustained softness could limit operating leverage and make future expansion increasingly dependent on professional sales.

bear.t: Fading Inflation Benefit and Cost Pressure
bear.b: As tariff-related price benefits roll off, reported ticket and sales support should weaken, placing more emphasis on volume and market-share gains. Elevated store-level expenses may further constrain margin expansion if sales growth moderates.
